archive_18_001.speaker: narrator
archive_18_001.text: Yue woke on day one hundred and nineteen to wagon wheels sounding below the turn. Her weekly rest had begun, and the receiving roster did not include her. She lay still while the yard bell gave its ordinary arrival notice. A few weeks earlier, she would have gone downstairs to prove the archive could rely on her. Now Tan, the cook and their assigned workers were already there. She could hear the cook asking about an oil jar. Yue pulled the blanket towards her chin and decided that question belonged to the cook.

archive_18_002.speaker: narrator
archive_18_002.text: The last spring consignment arrived through the repaired carriage approach after its morning loaded-route check. The driver held the departure and intermediate receipts in a dry cover and waited at the marked point until the yard was ready. Tan took the charcoal checks; the cook and her assistant took the complete food components. The archive workers moved the accepted loads to their dry assigned places. Nobody asked the five mules to appear again simply because they had been memorable. This journey had used balanced wagons and the road which the district had actually reopened.

archive_18_003.speaker: narrator
archive_18_003.text: From her window, Yue saw one driver stroke a wheel hub before beginning the unloading. She wondered whether it was superstition or a temperature check and resisted turning the moment into a question she needed to solve today. Luo helped keep the waiting space clear. He Xi passed on his paid local route, waved towards the window and kept going. His family had their own breakfast. The archive yard looked busy enough to continue without the person watching above it, a sight she found more reassuring than an invitation to help.

archive_18_004.speaker: narrator
archive_18_004.text: The receiving checks accepted four hundred and eighty-three food shares, including the three free replacements for the first carrier's rejected shares. Forty sound five-kilogram charcoal sacks and fifty dry cooking bundles passed their checks. The food components matched the cook's accepted specification. The driver signed the actual delivery condition, and the cook sent him towards the carrier's arranged village lodging for his own meal. The winter pantry acquired its balance in real objects, which made the shelves smell briefly of fresh wrapping rather than the familiar old store.

archive_18_005.speaker: narrator
archive_18_005.text: The complete spring order now stood at six hundred accepted food shares, forty-eight charcoal sacks and sixty cooking bundles across the two actual deliveries. Its revised price was five hundred and thirty-two copper, including the split transport. The authorised spring contingency transfer enlarged the goods allocation by thirty-two. The lower treasurer paid five hundred and thirty-two against both signed receipts. Two hundred and eighty remained reserved for Yue's accepted extension, sixty for spring qualified work and twenty-eight in spring contingency. The goods arrived before stock ran out. Tan closed the pending page and opened use tags.

archive_18_006.speaker: narrator
archive_18_006.text: Dai took the completed receipt upstairs but left it outside Yue's door for later reading. She did not knock to turn a rest morning into a successful meeting. The sound of her steps faded, and Yue fell asleep again. In the dream, the archive's shelves were empty bowls which the fish tried to sell as windows. She woke laughing without knowing which part had been funny. Sun would certainly refuse to improve the dream into a properly attributed story. Yue put it in her own notebook with no claim that it revealed anything about rain.

archive_18_007.speaker: narrator
archive_18_007.text: At midday she went to the residential pot, where the ordinary resident share had been issued for her rest day like any other paid calendar day. The onions were smaller than those in the first consignment and tasted much the same. Tan had washed her hands and looked tired enough to enjoy neither a lesson nor a compliment. Yue asked whether the driver had been checking the hub's temperature. Tan said yes, then asked why she was inspecting people from bed. Yue said the question had waited until lunch. Tan accepted that as progress and passed the bowl.

archive_18_008.speaker: tan_ke
archive_18_008.text: All the goods passed. Three replacement shares, forty sacks and fifty bundles. You can read the receipt later. At present I want somebody to say something which cannot be entered as a useful verification. Tell me about the plum shopkeeper. Luo has explained the carrier's timetable twice, and I am beginning to think the wagon may come back merely to correct his account.

archive_18_009.speaker: narrator
archive_18_009.text: Yue told her about the shopkeeper saying plums could be eaten by an undecided person. Tan said that was an expensive professional consultation and asked what the plum cost. Yue refused to give her an itemised emotional account. Luo, arriving with his own resident bowl, declared that the refusal should have a file number. Dai told him to eat before the pot cooled. For several minutes the room was only a place where people ate, each capable of becoming unbearable in a different familiar way.

archive_18_010.speaker: narrator
archive_18_010.text: The workshop owner came to the public desk that afternoon without trying to interrupt Yue upstairs. He brought the retained customer copy for the lost cabinet pattern and the stopped-room notice. His association's assessor would arrive on the next safe local inspection round. He wanted help identifying the copy's actual dimensions before deciding what to remake. The assistant arranged the ordinary advisory appointment and asked him to bring the commissioning slip if it survived. He had it in the front tray. One line on that slip would make the copy's date much easier to interpret.

archive_18_011.speaker: narrator
archive_18_011.text: He also had a proposed repair estimate from the qualified joiner. The damaged loft and packing-room partition could be made safe without rebuilding the whole workshop, but the heater needed a separate approved guard and inspection. The owner disliked having two estimates when one room had burned. The joiner said a floor and a charged heating frame were two different kinds of thing even when both inconvenienced the same man. The owner accepted the split and asked for the earliest safe work sequence. He had paid the current wages and lodging; now he needed work which could resume.

archive_18_012.speaker: narrator
archive_18_012.text: He Xi's father spent that afternoon in his own room under the clinician's recovery plan. He asked his wife to describe her kitchen shift instead of the workshop. She told him about a pot lid which had disappeared and been found exactly where she had put it. He laughed too hard, coughed and had to stop. She waited, then said the pot lid would remain available for his amusement tomorrow. Their son heard them from the doorway and went out to finish his paid parcel route without correcting the story into a medical warning.

archive_18_013.speaker: narrator
archive_18_013.text: Sun took the umbrella notebook to the village room's quiet corner. The room attendant let her sit there during an ordinary open interval because Sun preferred its light to her own kitchen's late shade. She paid the posted small use fee from her own writing money and began the third page. The umbrella's owner had now promised to stitch the hole shut using a fish's advice. Sun crossed the fish out. She did not want one successful animal to seize every story. The attendant asked whether anybody in the new story would manage to pay the room bill.

archive_18_014.speaker: sun_nian
archive_18_014.text: The umbrella may pay by sheltering the room from its owner, who talks too much. I have not decided whether that is a fair rate. If you charge by the word, I shall go home and write in bad light. If you charge by the chair, I have already paid. You may laugh at the umbrella for free, since I have allowed it to become rude in a public room.

archive_18_015.speaker: narrator
archive_18_015.text: The attendant laughed, then left Sun alone with the page. Outside, children dragged a little board through the old snow and declared it a wagon capable of crossing every bridge. Their game had neither loads nor deadlines until one child insisted the passengers should get off before the steep turn. Sun watched the quarrel without turning it into the day's fourth lesson. She gave the umbrella a passenger who hated sunshine, then stopped writing when the room's light shifted. Three new pages existed. They were still hers to improve or abandon.

archive_18_016.speaker: narrator
archive_18_016.text: In her own rest evening, Yue opened Dai's receipt copy and read the actual quantities. She was glad the first incomplete carrier had been made whole without an argument about gratitude. She put the supply account with the employment papers she had permission to retain for her work and left the home letter apart. The goods supported the spring term she had chosen, but the term would still need fifty-six days of people waking, eating, working and resting. She closed the folder, then took the plums out for an ordinary private supper addition.

archive_18_017.speaker: narrator
archive_18_017.text: Tan declined another plum because the first had made her face disobedient. Luo accepted one and immediately tried to look scholarly about its sourness. Dai laughed at him so suddenly that he nearly swallowed the stone. The cook confiscated the remaining stones before someone added them to a drawer of unidentified specimens. Yue thought the archive had acquired the right sort of rest-day result: nobody needed her command, the pot had enough components and her friends had made fools of themselves with a fruit she bought. She went to bed before the late round rang.

archive_18_018.speaker: narrator
archive_18_018.text: The mutual-loss assessor arrived on day one hundred and twenty with a dry ledger and a pair of boots which she refused to polish until the inspection was finished. She went first to the safe front room with the owner and foreman, then viewed the closed areas from the permitted positions. The membership record held by her association confirmed the workshop's current cover. A burned policy copy in the rear drawer did not erase that separate record. The owner looked relieved enough to begin listing the six lost patterns before she had finished describing the building damage.

archive_18_019.speaker: narrator
archive_18_019.text: The policy covered the declared room and heating equipment within its assessed limit. It did not price the owner's reputation or pretend a lifetime's design work could be replaced by the value of its paper. The assessor approved a provisional thirty-copper payment against a maximum forty-five for the inspected covered loss, with the balance subject to the completed safe repair records. The six original drawings remained an actual loss outside that simple sum. She wrote them in the condition account where they belonged. The owner read the difference and asked whether she had ever kept a drawing herself.

archive_18_020.speaker: narrator
archive_18_020.text: She said yes, then asked him to show the qualified repair estimate. He had twenty-five copper left after the earned wages, reserved worker lodging and He Xi's father's two paid recovery days at the agreed one-and-a-half-copper daily rate. The new thirty-copper provisional payment brought present repair money to fifty-five. The qualified plan cost forty-two: fourteen in floor and partition materials, twelve in labour, six for the heater guard, four for its inspection and six for a fresh feed stone after approval. Thirteen would remain. He could begin a safe partial reopening without inventing a fully recovered business.

archive_18_021.speaker: narrator
archive_18_021.text: He stared at the six-copper feed stone line. The old stone had spent all six units in the incident, four as working heat and two through the ground receiver. He knew its loss was ordinary use and had nevertheless been hoping somebody might call it salvageable. Tan, present for the equipment comparison, asked whether he wanted the keeper to inspect the cold empty fitting before ordering the replacement. He said yes. The keeper did so and confirmed the empty state. The owner crossed salvage from his note and looked as though a small personal fantasy had been taken away.

archive_18_022.speaker: tan_ke
archive_18_022.text: You still have the fitting. You still have the remote circuit which worked. The new guard must pass its own check before a fresh stone goes near it. Start with those things. I can help compare the surviving cabinet copy during our agreed desk interval. I cannot make the stone full by giving the empty one a kinder name.

archive_18_023.speaker: narrator
archive_18_023.text: The assessor counted the thirty copper at the village association desk, issued its receipt and retained the inspection reference. It was actual money before the owner paid the first accepted repair bill. She would return for the completed covered work and remaining claim, not write a cheque for a roof nobody had yet made safe. The owner paid the joiner's ordered materials from the present fifty-five and signed the work sequence. Outside, the closed loft window looked smaller in daylight. The room could be repaired, though the papers it had held would not be persuaded by an invoice.

archive_18_024.speaker: narrator
archive_18_024.text: At the archive's public advisory table, the retained customer copy lay beneath a dry weight. It showed a cabinet front and lid drawn before the maker changed the final hinge. The commissioning slip identified that earlier version. The owner had almost forgotten the alteration because customers remembered the finished cabinet, while his own working sheets had carried the sequence. Tan asked where the finished cabinet was. It stood in the customer's village dining room. The customer could allow a present measurement visit if asked; no archive diagram could grant entry to another person's house.

archive_18_025.speaker: narrator
archive_18_025.text: He Xi carried the actual request on a paid local loop. The customer agreed to an appointment after her household's midday meal and named the craftsman she would admit. She did not agree to a group arriving without notice to admire the only unburned evidence. The owner went with his trained fitter and a clean measuring cord. Yue heard their departure time from the ordinary desk update and remained at her own assigned work. The safe visit needed the people who could measure a cabinet, not everybody who cared about whether the archive's advice had helped.

archive_18_026.speaker: narrator
archive_18_026.text: The owner returned with current measurements and a small correction to the customer copy. The final hinge was narrower, and the maker had raised the lid stop after fitting. Those observations supported a present reconstruction of that cabinet, with the customer-copy date and visit date identified. They did not recover the burned working corrections as original ink. Tan marked the new drawing current reconstruction and named the actual contributors. The owner frowned at the heading, then asked whether the future buyer would mind. Tan said he could describe the cabinet honestly and let the buyer decide.

archive_18_027.speaker: narrator
archive_18_027.text: Luo helped the assistant complete a cotton-house applicant issue during his second paid training interval. The descendant had brought the missing household connection record, and the winter deputy checked it against the actual appendix. The requested service fields stayed within the granted scope. Luo compared the relevant row, complete heading and permission reference without issuing it on his own. The assistant approved and recorded the handover. No missing signature was hidden by the source-match stamp. The descendant took the page to the competent desk, and Luo watched someone leave with useful evidence made through the process he had once bypassed.

archive_18_028.speaker: luo_zhimo
archive_18_028.text: The new procedure is better than the old condition. I helped ask for it after making a bad issue, and I should have helped ask before. I do not want us to pretend that every future question will fit this appendix. When one does not, I will put that stopped request where the approving person can see it. I have discovered that a visible stopped request is less lonely than carrying the whole exception in my own head.

archive_18_029.speaker: narrator
archive_18_029.text: The assistant said the stopped request still required somebody to act. She would not let him make a useful rack sound like a finished remedy. He laughed, accepted the correction and took the next admitted public lookup. She had become willing to answer him directly rather than cautiously preserve his pride. The board observer noted the actual training work for the coming review. Luo did not need to manufacture an error in order to demonstrate recovery. He needed to handle an ordinary request with all its present evidence, which he had done.

archive_18_030.speaker: narrator
archive_18_030.text: Yue used the afternoon to revise the pupils' date question. She had imagined teaching a source as a thing one could verify and then rely on. The cabinet copy made that answer too simple. Its earlier lid was accurately drawn and no longer matched the finished lid. A present measurement could help a different task. She drew a little box with an opening which changed after fitting, then labelled its stages with invented dates. The prop was plain enough that a child could ask the useful question without needing to know anything about a workshop fire.

archive_18_031.speaker: narrator
archive_18_031.text: He Xi collected the school cover and examined the drawn box. He said its hinge resembled Nettle's offended ear. Yue told him his mule drawing had become influential and should charge for its contributions. He asked whether to put that in the school lesson. She allowed the attributed joke and asked him not to bill pupils for an animal's opinion. He grinned, then asked whether a current source date mattered to a courier as much as an address. She handed him the invented slip and asked which date he wanted on a route.

archive_18_032.speaker: narrator
archive_18_032.text: He chose the current road check rather than the old bridge opening. Then he asked whether every public source ought to be checked again each day. Yue said the question depended on the task, and they could compare a route with an old song's text at school. He disliked receiving an answer which became another question. She asked whether his own price lesson had already solved the wrong-address case. He said no. Their conversation ended in a mutual refusal to pretend somebody else had a simpler profession.

archive_18_033.speaker: narrator
archive_18_033.text: The joiner began the safe floor work on day one hundred and twenty-one. The closed areas stayed closed except to the qualified repair team. The owner kept ordinary light bench work in the cleared front room, paying its actual accepted tasks from incoming commissions. He Xi's father returned only after a fresh clinical assessment limited him to short fitted-piece intervals with rest. He complained about stopping just when a piece began to make sense. The foreman told him to write its current measure before stopping so the next interval would not begin by arguing with his own memory.

archive_18_034.speaker: narrator
archive_18_034.text: That evening he brought home a scrap with three measurements and one badly drawn lid. His wife studied the drawing and asked whether the customer had bought a cupboard or a boat. He said the lid was the useful part. She told him to keep the scrap dry and finish his meal before improving his sketch. He Xi had nearly asked to see the recovery allowance receipt; instead he asked whether the new hinge moved cleanly. His father answered for several minutes, and their rented room filled with the sound of a man describing work he still wanted to do.

archive_18_035.speaker: narrator
archive_18_035.text: On the morning of day one hundred and twenty-two, Luo dressed before the hall stove had warmed the room. He chose the brown robe he wore for ordinary issue work, then changed it because its cuff needed mending. The smaller decision irritated him more than the review appointment. He had prepared every requested record and slept badly imagining somebody asking for the one he had forgotten. At breakfast the cook passed him the mending basket without comment. He repaired the cuff while his porridge cooled and carried the finished robe upstairs.

archive_18_036.speaker: narrator
archive_18_036.text: The board's two appointed reviewers arrived during its authorised morning sitting. Dai attended as the custodian who had recorded the breach; a separate senior clerk chaired the decision so she did not judge her own handling alone. The winter deputy joined by the agreed local appointment, with the cotton owner's current written appendix in its cover. Yue brought her dated limited account and remained available for questions. The seamstress had agreed that the procedural dates could be considered. Her household particulars stayed under the cover she had chosen.

archive_18_037.speaker: narrator
archive_18_037.text: The reviewer asked Luo what he now understood differently about the day he had issued the copy. He began with the fund deadline and stopped when she raised one finger. She knew the deadline. She wanted the step he had taken. He said he had reproduced an entrusted private row without the owner's required permission, knowing that source accuracy did not provide it. The deputy asked whether the later appendix changed that answer. Luo said no. His voice sounded flatter than he intended, but nobody asked him to make remorse more picturesque.

archive_18_038.speaker: narrator
archive_18_038.text: They examined the paid training records from the ninety-fourth day and the one hundred and twentieth. The first had covered source authority and reproduction terms; the second had followed an applicant through an actual permitted issue, including the deputy's approval reference. The supervising clerk had observed both and recorded where Luo had needed a prompt. He had omitted a return-address field in the second exercise, corrected it before issue and entered the correction. Luo disliked the small failure appearing beside his larger one. The reviewer said that hiding it would have made the training less useful.

archive_18_039.speaker: luo_zhimo
archive_18_039.text: I used to think an issue record should look as if the person at the desk had never hesitated. People waited, and I wanted the waiting to end. Now I have a page showing that I stopped to ask whether an address was mine to copy. It is untidy. The applicant still left with what she needed. I am trying to become a clerk who can tolerate that sort of untidiness before doing something more damaging to avoid it.

archive_18_040.speaker: narrator
archive_18_040.text: The reviewers tested the actual next application under the winter appendix. Luo identified the person's admitted purpose, checked the permitted row and obtained the deputy's approval reference before preparing the named extract. He did not recopy neighbouring fields merely because they were visible. The supervising clerk compared the draft with the source and asked the applicant to confirm the receiving address privately. The applicant corrected one character. Luo changed it, read it back and placed the issue under its proper authority. The reviewers watched a completed task rather than a recital of ideal behaviour.

archive_18_041.speaker: narrator
archive_18_041.text: Their written decision restored Luo's ordinary clerk issue role from that afternoon, subject to the normal source checks. It did not give him independent authority to approve private reproduction. The cotton appendix still required the owner's appointed deputy and ended with its stated term. The earlier warning remained in the appropriate staff record. A public procedural notice described the restriction, training and actual review without identifying the applicant's private circumstances. Luo read it before it was pinned up. The notice was shorter than his fears and longer than he would once have considered necessary.

archive_18_042.speaker: narrator
archive_18_042.text: Dai asked him to examine her own catalogue correction during the next ordinary staff meeting. Luo almost made a joke about punishment being contagious, then saw that she meant the request. Her seven-year-old abbreviation had made an incomplete condition look complete. She had corrected its public description, but the approaching hearing would ask how the error had travelled through later references. He agreed to check the chain with the separate clerk rather than simply trust her new paragraph. They stood beside the meeting table for a moment, neither offering the other an acquittal.

archive_18_043.speaker: narrator
archive_18_043.text: Outside, Luo found Yue waiting near the stairs with the empty mending basket. She had taken it downstairs after his hurried breakfast and brought it back because the cook wanted her needles. He said the cuff was probably better examined than he was. Yue looked at the crooked stitches and said it had survived his attention, which was a modest favourable result. He laughed before he could decide whether the morning permitted laughter. They carried the basket down together. The public desk would reopen after the meal, and someone had already left a question about a boundary map.

archive_18_044.speaker: narrator
archive_18_044.text: That applicant did not know why Luo was unusually slow over the first page. She wanted to establish whether her old lane came under the southern drainage assessment. He showed her the public map's date and asked which current notice she had received. She produced a crumpled bill with a new district heading. The source could explain the older boundary; the current collecting desk needed to answer the charge. Luo wrote the actual referral and marked the unresolved difference. She thanked him for giving her somewhere precise to be annoying. He thought it a respectable use of an archive.

archive_18_045.speaker: narrator
archive_18_045.text: A letter from Yue's mother arrived that afternoon through He Xi's paid local delivery. Its outside carried two rain spots from a lower relay shelter, carefully dried before the cover was closed. Yue signed for it and took it to her own room during a break. Her mother had received the extension decision and asked whether Yue was certain she wanted another spring away. She also reported a cracked cooking lid, a neighbour's marriage and an argument over whose chicken had eaten seed meant for somebody else. Home had continued without arranging every event around its absent daughter.

archive_18_046.speaker: narrator
archive_18_046.text: Her mother did not demand an immediate return. She wanted a likely date so she could stop telling relatives that Yue would appear whenever a mountain finished being troublesome. Yue laughed at the sentence, then read the next one more slowly. Her mother missed hearing somebody answer from the other room before asking what had happened. The longing was ordinary and inconvenient, with no moral claim strong enough to settle a choice. Yue placed the letter beside her accepted appointment page. The dates could answer one part; they could not answer what it felt like to wait.

archive_18_047.speaker: lin_yue
archive_18_047.text: I can write that the term ends on the one hundred and eighty-eighth day. I cannot write that I shall never choose another road after it. Mother has not asked for that promise. I keep hearing it in her questions because a final promise would make me feel less divided. She has asked for a date, an account of my leg and whether I eat properly. Those are questions I can answer without inventing a daughter who no longer wants anything beyond the next room.

archive_18_048.speaker: narrator
archive_18_048.text: She wrote the actual end date and explained that a later road journey would depend on the open route and her chosen work. Her calf had recovered for ordinary movement and assessed practice, with no reason to turn every day into a test. She described the public lesson preparation and the cook's refusal to accept cabbage as prophecy. She did not include the seamstress's private account or Sun's unfinished umbrella sentences. Her mother could know her life without receiving other people's lives folded inside it. The letter went into her own paid outgoing envelope, ready for the next safe relay.

archive_18_049.speaker: narrator
archive_18_049.text: Dai's reply arrived separately on the one hundred and twenty-third day. Her daughter could receive her from the one hundred and seventy-sixth through the one hundred and seventy-ninth, with travel on the surrounding days if the road actually opened. She had made room by moving two work appointments and asked Dai to bring the spectacles she kept refusing to replace. Dai read the offer twice and booked the proposed absence from day one hundred and seventy-four through one hundred and eighty-one. The board's cover approval still required a checked spring route before departure.

archive_18_050.speaker: narrator
archive_18_050.text: Tan saw Dai measuring the old spectacles against the letter's smallest writing. She asked whether the daughter had found a suitably narrow table for her mother's papers. Dai said the daughter had asked for her mother, not an archive inspection. Tan waited. Dai removed the spectacles and admitted she had considered taking a catalogue draft to explain why she had stayed so long. Tan said a daughter probably knew what work looked like when it had occupied sixty-one years of somebody's face. Dai folded the letter carefully and left the draft on the desk.

archive_18_051.speaker: narrator
archive_18_051.text: The warmer interval began that day, with the cook and keeper agreeing to reduce the hall's charcoal issue to a half sack while conditions allowed. Nights still froze, and the watcher's road notices remained winter notices. Snow loosened from the eaves in slow clumps, falling into the marked yard area while people used the other doorway. Yue heard the first wet thud during her last shelf round. It sounded like a sack dropped by a careless porter. The porter in the yard looked upwards and accused the roof of copying his work.

archive_18_052.speaker: narrator
archive_18_052.text: On the one hundred and twenty-fourth morning, Tan visited the repaired workshop front room to compare the customer's current hinge with the reconstructed drawing. The customer brought the cabinet itself on a sound handcart, complaining that everyone remembered the fire while he had been living with the drawer that caught. Tan asked him to open it three times. On the third attempt, it stuck at the same small twist. The front copy showed an earlier hinge arrangement; his dated repair receipt described the later change. She labelled both stages before asking the joiner to measure the present fitting.

archive_18_053.speaker: narrator
archive_18_053.text: The joiner found that the new safety guard would block the old tool-rest position. He could move the rest and preserve the guard's clearance, but it would change the operator's reach. The foreman tried the ordinary unpowered posture and felt the difference in his shoulder. Tan asked him to name that discomfort before somebody wrote a beautiful plan nobody could use. They adjusted the bench height within its rated setting and tested the reach again. The corrected drawing acquired three grubby fingerprints and one clear measurement. The customer asked whether his drawer might now become part of history.

archive_18_054.speaker: narrator
archive_18_054.text: He Xi's father worked a short assessed interval beside the foreman, then stopped as his clinical limit required. The unfinished piece annoyed him. He wrote its measurement and let another worker carry it to the rack. His son arrived with the owner's correspondence and saw the handover without making a speech about recovery. The father asked whether the route still passed the lamp shop. He Xi said it did, if a customer actually lived beyond the lamp shop. The father nodded, accepting the teasing answer. A family could begin talking about routes again without pretending earlier absences had never existed.

archive_18_055.speaker: narrator
archive_18_055.text: At the archive, the trustees' clerk requested a fresh catalogue chain for the house hearing. The original condition, later continuation and current abbreviated entries would need to be distinguished in the receiving bundle. Dai authorised the lawful extracts under the parties' established access and asked the clerk to state which present office would examine them. A competent registry appointment was being arranged for spring, after participants could travel safely. The request was preparation, not a hearing date confirmed by wish. Yue fetched the earlier dispatch references and discovered how many pages a single omitted condition had touched.

archive_18_056.speaker: narrator
archive_18_056.text: The chain included Dai's own abbreviated description, Luo's earlier returned work copy and the later copies requested by the trustee. None changed the surviving endorsed continuation. Several had made it harder to find. Dai wrote the distinction plainly and signed the account of her catalogue step. Luo attached his source route and correction reference without disguising the returned wrapper mistake. The clerk thanked them for a bundle which explained itself. Dai found the thanks uncomfortable; it had arrived too close to what she would once have called a tidy catalogue. She returned to checking the last page.

archive_18_057.speaker: narrator
archive_18_057.text: Sun brought her umbrella notebook only to show Tan the cover's new paper sleeve. She did not offer the story for the archive's hearing exhibit, and no one had asked her to. The sleeve had been made from a shop offcut with a horse's nose printed on its edge. Sun liked the nose because the umbrella owner was becoming smug and needed company. Tan said the horse looked as though it disapproved of rain. Sun said every sensible horse did. They sat beside the residential window while the hall's quieter half-sack fire settled into an even warmth.

archive_18_058.speaker: sun_nian
archive_18_058.text: I am thinking of making the umbrella insist on staying open indoors. Its owner will object that this is inconvenient. The umbrella will say that it has spent years being opened only when somebody else dislikes the sky. I do not yet know whether that is a good argument. The horse on the cover thinks nothing of it. I may let the owner win for one afternoon and find out what the umbrella does afterwards. Stories are tiresome when every objection arrives already carrying its answer.

archive_18_059.speaker: narrator
archive_18_059.text: The teacher asked for a later reading once the page was ready. Sun said she would discuss its scope and payment when she knew whether she wanted to read it. He accepted the answer and asked whether the horse could appear in the children's drawing lesson meanwhile. She permitted the sleeve's printed nose to be copied for that ordinary purpose, provided nobody attributed the shop horse to her pen. He said it would receive a modest and accurate introduction. She told him not to make accuracy sound like an animal suffering from a long illness.

archive_18_060.speaker: narrator
archive_18_060.text: On the evening of day one hundred and twenty-five, the cook closed the week's actual issue sheet. Seven days had used seventy resident food shares and seven cooking bundles, with no additional archive meal guests. Four colder days had taken four charcoal sacks; the three mild days had taken one and a half. After the accepted bulk delivery, the store held seven hundred and thirty-nine and a half food shares, sixty usable charcoal sacks and eighty-eight and a half dry cooking bundles. Ten residents remained on the meal roll. Tan checked the arithmetic before signing the count.

archive_18_061.speaker: narrator
archive_18_061.text: The count left time rather than abundance without limit. Food still had to reach the remaining winter days and accepted spring term, and any new guests would need actual entries. Dai placed the signed sheet beside the paid supply receipts. The cook put tomorrow's beans to soak and told everyone to stop admiring figures long enough to carry the washed bowls. Yue carried them into the kitchen. The window showed a narrow line of dripping eaves against snow, and the room smelled of the meal they had actually eaten.

archive_18_062.speaker: narrator
archive_18_062.text: Before bed, Luo repaired the robe's second cuff. Yue found him at the residential table with the same basket and asked whether the board had ordered matching stitches. He said the first cuff had made the second look ambitious in the wrong direction. Dai passed through carrying her daughter's letter in a plain cover. She asked whether he could spare the needle when he finished. Her travelling sleeve had a loose seam. Luo handed over the basket without asking what the journey would prove, and Dai sat down to mend.
